concerns.text: FR-002 states the permutation test uses a *target‑permutation* (shuffling the response variable) to compare the Full Model against a Null Model. A target‑permutation destroys the signal for both models, so it cannot isolate the contribution of interaction features. This contradicts the intended purpose of testing whether interactions add predictive value.

SC-002 requires a permutation test that directly compares the Full Model (with interactions) to the Null Model (without interactions) and assesses significance (α ≤ 0.05). This conflicts with FR‑002’s description of a target‑permutation test, creating an irreconcilable requirement.

The document refers to the three user journeys both as “User Story 1/2/3” and as “US‑1, US‑2, US‑3” in acceptance scenarios and success criteria. The identifiers US‑1/2/3 are never defined, leading to unresolved cross‑references.

SC‑007 defines the empirical p‑value as the proportion of shuffled ΔRMSE ≤ observed, i.e., the lower tail of the null distribution. Elsewhere (SC‑002) the test is described as an upper‑tail comparison (ΔRMSE ≥ observed). The opposite directions are inconsistent within the spec.
References to “US‑1” in SC‑007 (and elsewhere) are undefined; the spec only contains numbered User Stories without a US‑# scheme, causing a silent scope shift and broken traceability.
